definition: the order I want one in, from adjusting itself down to nothing at all

settled:
A tool that matches the dose to the load beats one that forces on or off, even though working it takes something from me.

I adjust a tool while it runs, on a live signal, whatever its cost shape: an AirPod part out, clothes broken loose, the blanket swapped mid-sleep.

Whether it belongs on by default depends on which way the error is expensive. Where being under-protected costs me far more than being over-protected, the tool runs at full and I take relief downward by hand. The ear tips and the tight clothes both work that way.

Where the two errors cost about the same, or over-protection costs more, the tool correctly waits off until I reach for it. The weighted blanket is the case that showed me the rule has that edge.

title: How I Pick A Sensory Tool
